https://nineoclock.ro/romania-adopts-eme.text: ABOUT US NINE O’CLOCK STAFF 2024 COMMERCIAL OFFER – 2026 Subscribe to the Nine O’Clock 2026 CONTACT Special price offer 2026 with a 50% discount The Romanian Government, during an extraordinary meeting, adopted the “Decision on the Adoption of Safety Measures on the Electricity Market”, creating the legal framework for interventions aimed at safeguarding the operation of the National Power System. Thus, the necessary legal framework has been created for C.N.T.E.E. Transelectrica S.A. , through the National Energy Dispatch Centre , to order, until August 31, 2026, a series of safety measures if developments in the National Power System make them necessary. These measures could be implemented during periods when an electricity deficit is recorded, in the following order of priority: Increasing technological system reserves at generation units capable of operating on alternative fuels, with a view to using them; Starting generating units held in technical reserve and available to the National Energy Dispatch Centre; Reducing or cancelling available interconnection capacity in the export direction; Reducing or cancelling notified electricity exchanges in the export direction; Gradually limiting electricity consumption between 19:00 and 23:00, under the conditions established by the Electricity Consumption Limitation Regulation, which covers only large electricity-consuming economic operators and does not apply to household consumers. The Government stressed that household consumers are not targeted by the consumption limitation mechanism. The measures are designed to provide Transelectrica, through the National Energy Dispatch Centre, with the necessary tools to maintain the balance between electricity production and consumption and safeguard the stability of Romania’s National Power System. The measures may be applied until August 31, 2026, depending on developments in the national electricity system. The Government said that the measures will be implemented only if the evolution of the National Power System makes them necessary. https://www.rferl.org/a/ukraine-sbu-atta.text: Accessibility links Skip to main content Skip to main Navigation Skip to Search Print Options: Images Multimedia Embedded Content Comments News US Envoys Arrive In Moscow As Russia Continues To Pound Ukraine By RFE/RL's Ukrainian Service September 04, 2026 17:52 CET Updated September 05, 2026 12:36 CET US Envoys Arrive In Moscow As Russia Continues To Pound Ukraine Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google A motorcade carrying US President Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner leaves Vnukovo International Airport in Moscow on September 5. Listen to this article 8 min This audio is automated Learn more US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have landed in Moscow as part of the latest White House attempt to end Russia's war against its neighbor, with the two diplomats set to visit Kyiv afterward. Their arrival, reported by Reuters and TASS, marks a rare development in effectively stalled negotiations between Kyiv and Moscow came as Russian forces launched a fresh wave of attacks across Ukraine. Earlier, US President Donald Trump said Washington had "an idea for peace," adding that his envoys were "bringing with them a proposal to end the war." "We sent them over to see whether or not we can get something done, and there may be a good chance that we'll do it," Trump told reporters at the White House on September 4 without providing details. SEE ALSO: Alleged Confession Video Raises More Questions About Ukrainian Security Agencies' Shoot-Out Responding to increasing concerns in the West that Russian President Vladimir Putin could attack a NATO member to test the alliance's resolve, Trump again said he doesn't believe the Kremlin leader is planning such a move. "I speak to him. I know him very well. Putin's not looking to attack NATO territory," Trump said. Zelenskyy said on September 4 that "today it has been clearly determined that American representatives will be in Ukraine and in Russia in the coming days" and he called for a pause in air strikes by both sides to facilitate any meetings. He added that the US team had informed him that Witkoff and Kushner would first visit Kyiv on September 6, a day after their talks in Moscow. Previously, a US official had confirmed to RFE/RL that Witkoff and Kushner would travel to Moscow and Kyiv "in the coming days." Zelenskyy Calls For Pause In Air Strikes Zelenskyy said Ukrainian forces would "ensure the normal functioning of Russia airspace so that the negotiators can arrive there safely" and demanded that Moscow reciprocate. "There will be no air strikes from our side, and Russia must also refrain from conducting air strikes for the time needed to hold these negotiations." The visit would come just days after a Russia drone strike hit the headquarters of Ukraine's domestic security service -- known as the SBU and a key agency that would be responsible for the US envoys' safety during a visit. "Unfortunately, a Russian drone hit the central building of the SBU on Volodymyrska Street in Kyiv, opposite the St. Sophia Cathedral," Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Telegram , referring to the main building of the domestic intelligence agency. SEE ALSO: How Much Can Ukraine Disrupt Civilian Flights In Russia? "The drone was aimed directly at the office of the head of the security service in that building," he said, adding that SBU chief Oleksandr Poklad was not pressent at the time. Prior to calling for a pause in air strikes, Zelenskyy said he had ordered Poklad to "adequately, noticeably and, if possible, to mirror" the Russians' actions "when everything is prepared. " Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said at least seven people were injured in the strike. It was not immediately disclosed if SBU members were among the injured. The normal high-security measures around the sensitive building prevented journalists from viewing the damage to the sprawling site. Heavy black smoke was seen above the city center following the attack. Despite Zelenskyy's call for a mutual pause ahead of a fresh round of diplomacy, Russia continued to target places across Ukraine on September 5, killing at least four people in Ukraine's industrial city of Kamianske in the Dnipropetrovsk region. Russian attacks were also reported in the Kyiv, Mykolayiv, and Poltava regions. The Ukrainian military said that, in its overnight strikes, Moscow used Iskander-M ballistic missiles and at least 167 drones, around half of which were jet-powered. SEE ALSO: Russia's Jet-Powered Drones: A Major New Threat To Ukraine Amid Speeding Arms Race Experts See 'Escalation' Heather A. Conley, a senior fellow at the American Enterprise Institute (AEI) and former deputy assistant secretary of state for the Bureau of European and Eurasian Affairs, said the attack signaled a ramping up of the Kremlin's air offensive against Ukraine. "This was a clear escalation of Russia as it follows along six days of intense bombing," she told RFE/RL. "I just believe they are they are accelerating their efforts just as they see Ukraine's drones and so-called long-range sanctions having a significant impact in Russia." Conley said the strike "absolutely contradicts" Putin's statement a day earlier suggesting that he is open to negotiations again. Tressa Guenov, former senior Pentagon and State Department official, told RFE/RL that Russia's "daytime strike on Ukraine’s SBU headquarters in Kyiv is part of an increasingly escalatory dynamic and mounting strikes against the capital." "One can guess that Moscow has always likely had plans on the shelf aimed at SBU targets, but hitting the headquarters today shows that Russia is willing to push new boundaries amidst an uncertain diplomatic situation." "For Ukraine, this attack is case in point why it needs urgent air defense interceptors," added Guenov, who is currently a senior fellow at the Scowcroft Center for Strategy and Security at the Atlantic Council. Attack Follows Street Gun Battle The attack comes two days after a dramatic shoot-out between the SBU and Ukraine's military intelligence agency, the HUR, on the streets of the capital. Their firefight erupted on September 2, but details of the incident and the reasons for the gun battle remain murky. SEE ALSO: Exclusive: A Secluded Russian Island May Hold Bioweapons Secrets Zelenskyy took swift action, firing the deputy heads of each organization on September 3 -- declaring "both agencies must be held accountable.” He'd previously said the gunfight was "disgraceful." The September 4 strike on the SBU building marked a continuation of Russia's campaign of daytime attack in and around Kyiv -- after four years of almost daily overnight strikes. It comes as Russia's ground offensive in eastern Ukraine stalls amid heavy losses on both sides. Russia has turned to launching jet-propelled drones capable of flying nearly twice as fast as older models, forcing Kyiv to adapt defenses in the battle against high-tech weapons and prompting leaders to plea for additional air defense weapons from Western partners. New Diplomatic Push The visits of the US envoys will mark their first visit to Ukraine since taking leading roles in the administration's efforts to end the war and come amid a renewed diplomatic push aimed at bringing a peace agreement in the increasingly bloody war. SEE ALSO: Ratcliffe's Moscow Warning: What We Know A Week Later, According To Ex-CIA Officers CIA Director John Ratcliffe on August 25 met with the heads of the Russian intelligence and security services in Moscow. The US spy agency did not disclose the full agenda, but the Kremlin said Ratcliffe did not meet with Putin. Ratcliffe reportedly warned Russian officials against attacking or testing NATO, with particular concern about the Baltic states of Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania. The AEI's Conley said that "it's absolutely unclear to me the next steps on US policy toward the conflict." "It's not clear if the US is willing to place pressure, more pressure on Russia," she said, citing confusion over a Russian sanctions bill currently on an uncertain course in the US Congress and uncertainty over potential licensing of the production of Patriot missiles to Ukraine. "There's just a lack of clarity right now on on how the US is planning to proceed," she added. Photograph: Jeff Moore/PA View image in fullscreen Russell Brand arriving at Southwark crown court with his wife, Laura Gallacher, on Tuesday. Photograph: Jeff Moore/PA UK news Russell Brand told woman to ‘clear up the mess you’ve made’ after alleged rape, court hears Woman says alleged assault at comedian’s London home was one of most painful experiences of her life Emine Sinmaz Tue 20 Oct 2026 14.22 EDT Last modified on Tue 20 Oct 2026 14.59 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A woman has said she “couldn’t speak or breathe” when Russell Brand raped her at his London townhouse after picking her out from a crowd after one of his gigs, a court has heard. She said the comedian looked “horrified” after the alleged attack so she assumed he would apologise but instead he told her: “Clear up the mess you’ve made.” The woman said she “tortured herself” in the years that followed because it was one of the “most painful experiences” of her life. Brand, 51, faces three charges of rape, three of sexual assault and one of indecent assault against six women, in allegations spanning 10 years from 1999 to 2009. He denies all the charges and has pleaded not guilty. The TV personality sat upright in the dock as the woman’s video-recorded police interview was played to Southwark crown court on Tuesday. The woman told officers she was a “massive fan” of Brand and “giddy” to meet him after one of his stand-up performances at the Hammersmith Apollo in 2009. She alleged he pointed to her and said “you” before inviting her, her friend and a third young woman they did not know to have drinks with him. Brand’s security guard later invited the trio backstage where the woman performed oral sex on the actor but refused to have penetrative sex. By then, the woman’s friend had left, but Brand had sex on a sofa with the third woman, who was 19. The woman said she felt “awful” and “disgusting” when she left the dressing room, which is when Brand asked her why she had refused to have sex with him. She told him she had a boyfriend, to which he replied: “We don’t belong to anyone, we’re all free, the ownership of people is sort of what we’ve been sold.” View image in fullscreen The woman said Brand was ‘persuasive’ about her visiting his three-storey townhouse in Hampstead, west London. Photograph: Wenn Rights Ltd/Alamy Brand asked for her phone number and began messaging and calling her. She said he was “persuasive” about her visiting his three-storey townhouse in Hampstead, north-west London. Days later, the woman was picked up by Brand’s driver and taken to the star’s home knowing she would have sex with him. “I’ve really struggled for a really long time to accept what happened to me, because I went there knowingly and willingly,” she said. She alleged that when she arrived, Brand told her: “This is the best decision you’ve made.” But when they went to Brand’s bedroom, he ordered her to have a shower because her hair smelled “funny”, and made her brush her teeth. She said it made her feel “really dirty”, adding: “At the time it did feel like a thrilling thing to go to the house of this person I really fancied, and I loved comedy. But all those things didn’t feel that good.” View image in fullscreen The woman described Brand’s dark bedroom and ‘enormous’ bed. Photograph: Metropolitan Police She described his dark bedroom and “enormous” bed, and the distinctive black toilet paper in his ensuite bathroom. Pictures later shown to the jury showed a crucifix above his bed and black furnishings. The woman told how they had consensual vaginal sex but that she did not enjoy the experience, saying: “It felt very awkward. It didn’t matter who I was, and I just sort of wanted it to be over.” Then Brand anally raped the woman, she told police. “He didn’t give me a warning, he didn’t ask,” she said. “I don’t know how long it took for me between it going on and me asking him to stop. I don’t think it was very long. I felt like I couldn’t speak or breathe, the amount of pain.” She alleged she begged him to stop, at first really quietly and then more loudly, but Brand continued. She said he looked “absolutely fucking horrified” after the alleged attack, adding: “I thought he was going to say sorry … but actually what he said was: ‘You need to clear up the mess you’ve made.’” She said one of Brand’s aides later asked her to leave because the comedian had a gig. “The way I would describe that event to people after was that it was traumatic and that he hurt me and harmed me. And when I asked him to stop, he didn’t,” she said. She told the court she had gone to a sexual health clinic afterwards because she feared she had HIV, and she became unwell and anxious. “In the years that followed, if I spoke to people about it, it was was very much laced with ‘I shouldn’t have gone’, and I think I tortured myself because I think it was one of the most painful experiences I’d gone through.” Earlier on Tuesday, two women who have separately accused Brand of sexually assaulting them at work in front of his entourage gave evidence from behind a screen. The first woman said Brand laughed after “mauling” her by squeezing her breasts and kissing her sloppily while she was working at a radio station in 2004 or 2005. She told the court he “overpowered her with such strength” during the “violent” and “frenzied” attack that took place in the middle of her work day. She said she had “buried” the assault because there was such a culture of fear in the media in the 2000s and Brand was a “big star”. The second woman, who worked at Channel 4, said she was “repulsed” when Brand placed his head in her lap during a filming project after she was asked to give him a massage. She said Brand was with two men – named in court as Jack Bayles and Gareth Roy – during the alleged assault in 2009, which she reported to her line manager. The trial continues. https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text: Shayna Feinman. Photograph: Yavapai county sheriff's office View image in fullscreen Shayna Feinman. Photograph: Yavapai county sheriff's office Arizona A US woman feared dead was reported alive in Mexico. But cops now say that isn’t true Mexican police had said they found Shayna Feinman in Tijuana, raising the hopes of missing Arizonan’s family Ramon Antonio Vargas Wed 28 Oct 2026 06.00 EDT Last modified on Wed 28 Oct 2026 06.02 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Arizona authorities say their Mexican counterparts were resoundingly mistaken when they publicly claimed recently that they found alive a woman who was feared slain after disappearing in 2024 – a turn of events that her sister has called “turmoil” and “heartbreaking”. The case in question centers on Shayna Feinman, who was reported missing in rural Yavapai county, Arizona , in March 2024 at age 38. Authorities believe she was walking to an acquaintance’s home when she was last seen – but she never arrived or returned to her dog, as the Arizona news outlet KSAZ reported . An ensuing search turned up Feinman’s car abandoned near where she had been staying with her boyfriend, Cavett Richards, according to the station. Her wallet and identification reportedly were inside the vehicle, and her cellphone was ultimately recovered on nearby land. Although Feinman had not been found, the Yavapai county sheriff’s office subsequently charged Richards as well as a man named William DalCerro with second-degree murder, conspiracy and concealing a corpse in connection with her disappearance. But the charges were dismissed, a $20,000 reward being offered for information as authorities kept investigating the case. View image in fullscreen The person who Mexican officials thought was Shayna Feinman. Photograph: SSPCM Tijuana The secretariat for security and citizen protection in the Mexican municipality of Tijuana then delivered what initially appeared to be a startling update in Feinman’s case on Saturday, saying in a statement that she had been located in the city’s Encino neighborhood the previous day. The statement from the secretariat had a picture of the woman sitting in front of a desk atop which was a missing poster with Feinman’s information. It asserted without elaborating that investigators had confirmed Feinman’s identity, noting that her physical characteristics matched those listed in her missing person report. The woman had been put in protective custody while Tijuana authorities arranged for her to speak with the Feinman family and US consular officials, the statement said. The agency went so far as to post a link to its Saturday statement on a social media page belonging to Feinman’s sister, Kara. But both Kara Feinman and the Yavapai’s sheriff’s office met the Tijuana officials’ statement with evident skepticism. Kara told KSAZ in a story published on Monday that she was waiting for the Yavapai sheriff’s office “to know for certain” that Shayna had been found. Though she acknowledged the woman in the picture released by Tijuana officials had “similar physical attributes” to Shayna, Kara struck a cautious tone, telling KSAZ: “I can only hope and pray [for] good news – but right now, we have to be realistic.” Alexander brothers each sentenced to 30 years for drugging and raping dozens of women Read more Meanwhile, a sheriff’s office spokesperson told KSAZ that the agency was “aware of reports indicating that Shayna Feinman may have been located in Mexico” – but “at this time, the information remains unconfirmed”. “There is insufficient evidence to verify her identity,” Yavapai sheriff’s office spokesperson Paul Wick added to KSAZ. Wick said the sheriff’s office was “actively investigating the matter” and would provide an update as soon as one could be “confirmed and … released”. The Yavapai sheriff’s office published that update on Tuesday, when it said in a statement: “Today, US authorities confirmed to [office] detectives, utilizing physical evidence, that the individual located is not Shayna Feinman.” The sheriff’s office alluded to prior media reports “regarding the alleged discovery of Shayna Feinman” that “were published without official law enforcement confirmation” – before saying its “detectives continue to work diligently with [her] family during this stressful time”. Tijuana’s security and citizen protection secretariat did not immediately respond to a request for comment. In an interview with the Guardian on Tuesday, Kara Feinman said she believed the confusion about her sister possibly being in Tijuana initially stemmed from at least one concerned citizen who became convinced that she was there and made that known on social media. She described being guarded about that possibility, reluctantly opening her mind in light of the Tijuana secretariat’s claims – and then enduring cyberbullying online by users who harshly judged her for not reacting effusively enough to the ultimately false news that Shayna had been found alive. As she processed the reality that the search for the truth about her sister’s disappearance continued, Kara Feinman said her hope now was for those passionate about such investigations to realize how harmful it can be “jumping to conclusions without having all of the information” and then directing harsh words at the people most affected by those cases. “Words are stronger than people think, and kindness can go so far,” Kara Feinman said. “It’s been turmoil going through this. “It’s heartbreaking. It’s terrible, and I don’t wish this on anybody.” Explore more on these topics Arizona Mexico US crime Americas news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed World Europe US news Americas Asia Australia Middle East Africa Inequality Global development
